html:
The world order is significantly impacted today by a dramatic escalation of hostilities between the United States and Iran following the deaths of two US soldiers in Jordan. Both nations have launched new rounds of strikes, intensifying fears of a wider regional conflict.

US-Iran Escalation: The US launched new airstrikes to 'swiftly punish' Iran after two US soldiers were killed and one went missing in Jordan. US strikes reportedly hit an under-construction nuclear power plant in Iran, which the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) condemned as 'terrorist.' In response, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched missile and drone strikes on US military facilities in Jordan and two major US bases in Kuwait. Kuwait reported fires at power and water plants after Iranian attacks, with Bahrain and Israel also detecting Iranian missiles. Saudi Arabia and Syria condemned the Iranian attacks. Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei announced the suspension of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United States due to Washington's failure to adhere to commitments, a sentiment echoed by Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who stated the MoU proved the US president's signature 'worthless.' The IRGC Navy reported two ships had ‘accidents’ in the Strait of Hormuz after defying warnings, while US-backed plans for an Iraq-Syria oil pipeline gain urgency amidst Houthi threats to the Bab Al-Mandab blockade.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: Russia launched one of its largest ballistic missile attacks of the conflict on Ukrainian cities, including the capital, resulting in multiple casualties. Ukraine's air force reported 41 missiles and 125 attack drones used overnight, highlighting Ukraine's vulnerability due to a shortage of Patriot air defense munitions. Concurrently, Kyiv's forces continued their aerial campaign against Russian infrastructure, with drone attacks on Russian regions killing 8 and wounding over 60.

UK Political Transition & Geopolitics: Andy Burnham is preparing to lead Britain and is expected to face Trump, following the end of Keir Starmer's tenure a little more than two years after his 2024 general election victory. Burnham's approach is expected to be bolder but will stick to the Labour manifesto. Meanwhile, globally, the UK's nationalization of Chinese-owned British Steel is fueling a dispute with China, which is seeking damages for the move.

Global Economy and Trade: New EU border systems are tripling time at passport control, with Ryanair warning passengers to prepare for extended waits this summer. The EU has also implemented a ban on large companies destroying unsold clothes, accessories, and footwear to reduce waste. The escalating US-Iran conflict is impacting global energy, with US strikes cutting roads to the Strait of Hormuz and a renewed focus on bypassing the strait for oil transit.

International Security and Social Issues: Influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate were arrested in the US following further UK charges of rape and sex trafficking, with the UK seeking their extradition. In Cuba, prominent dissident artist Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara arrived in the US after being released from a five-year prison sentence on condition of exile. Globally, experts are warning that a rise in overseas surrogacy is increasing the risk of stateless babies, prompting calls for urgent international regulation of the practice.
